sentences.en: up in the ways that it usually would.

sentences.en: This is really often in response to some kind of threat that we have either been able to consciously detect or not.
sentences.zh: 这通常是对某种我们能够或无法有意识察觉到的威胁所做出的反应。

sentences.en: So according to what we know as polyvagal theory, our nervous system, when it sees or encounters a threat, follows a bit of a hierarchy.
sentences.zh: 根据我们所知的多迷走神经理论，当我们的神经系统看到或遇到威胁时，会遵循一定的层级机制。

sentences.en: First, we feel the urge to fight, then flight, so then run away.
sentences.zh: 首先，我们会感到战斗的冲动，然后是逃跑，也就是逃离现场。

sentences.en: And if neither of those is possible, if the danger feels inescapable, the body will shift into a freeze state or a shutdown state.
sentences.zh: 如果这两者都不可行，如果危险感觉无法逃避，身体就会转入冻结或关闭状态。

sentences.en: Dissociation is what is linked to that last pathway.
sentences.zh: 解离就与这最后一条路径有关。

sentences.en: It's also sometimes called the dorsal vagal state.
sentences.zh: 它有时也被称为背侧迷走神经状态。

sentences.en: Vagal meaning vagal nerve.
sentences.zh: 迷走指的是迷走神经。

sentences.en: This is the body's longest nerve.
sentences.zh: 这是人体内最长的神经。

sentences.en: It's the main pathway for regulating almost every system in our body, specifically our parasympathetic nervous system, which slows things down, shuts things off.
sentences.zh: 它是调节我们体内几乎所有系统的主要路径，特别是我们的副交感神经系统，它负责减缓生理节奏并关闭某些功能。

sentences.en: So when we experience dissociation, that state is triggered.
sentences.zh: 所以当我们经历解离时，这种状态就会被触发。

sentences.en: And that is what's creating this narrowing of awareness, this kind of detachment, lack of focus.
sentences.zh: 而这正是导致意识范围缩小、产生疏离感和注意力缺失的原因。

sentences.en: It's what causes our heart rate to drop.
sentences.zh: 它会导致我们的心率下降。

sentences.en: It's your nervous system basically saying, if I can't escape this, if I can't fight back against this, I'll just disconnect and maybe I'll survive with a few less emotional scars
sentences.zh: 这基本上是你的神经系统在说：如果我无法逃脱，如果我无法反抗，那我就切断连接，也许这样我就能少受一点情感创伤，

sentences.en: or at least with some energy for later.
sentences.zh: 或者至少能为以后保留一些能量。

sentences.en: When we look at the brain, neuroimaging studies will show that something fascinating happens during this process.
sentences.zh: 当我们观察大脑时，神经影像学研究显示，在这个过程中会发生一些迷人的现象。

sentences.en: When people with trauma-related or stress-related dissociation are reminded of distressing experiences

sentences.zh: 或处于压力状态时，我们大脑的警报系统——杏仁核，实际上往往会显示出

sentences.en: reduced activity compared to the intense activation that you would expect if someone was in a hyper aroused state.

sentences.en: So this gets kind of complicated here, but how people respond to trauma is different.

sentences.en: Some of them have hyper arousal.

sentences.en: So either you stay in this like cortisol fight or flight state and you are constantly hyper vigilant or alert, or some people go this way and they stay in this dissociative or hypo
sentences.zh: 你要么停留在这种皮质醇驱动的战斗或逃跑状态，时刻保持高度警惕或清醒，要么有些人会走向另一端，停留在这种解离或唤醒不足的状态，

sentences.en: In those cases, the part of our brain that would usually be like, everything's on fire, like run, run, run.

sentences.en: There's not as much communication going on.

sentences.en: Meanwhile, there's another part of our brain that is important for integrating emotions and for regulating emotions.

sentences.en: And during this state, it also goes quiet.

sentences.en: When that goes offline, we lose a lot of our sense of processing, rational processing, and a sense of like, I'm here and this is happening now.

sentences.en: We can lose our sense of being present, which is probably what's creating that weird feeling.

sentences.zh: 在专注于某项任务时失去时间感。

sentences.en: It might show up as zoning out a lot more, which people can get frustrated at you for, even though, you know, you're not deliberately trying to do it.
sentences.zh: 有些人将其标记为一种解离形式，或者仅仅是在高压时刻感到非常非常麻木。

sentences.en: Losing track of time whilst you're hyper-focusing on a task.

sentences.en: Like someone is, you know, bringing something to you or someone is putting something on your plate that like needs to be done immediately and you just operate.
sentences.zh: 这就像是一种奇怪的技能，我有几个患有多动症的朋友似乎就能做到这一点，当其他人都在抓狂时，他们却能应对自如。

sentences.en: You can just do it.
sentences.zh: 通常我会认为他们会有同样甚至更强烈的情绪反应，但他们只是变得超级专注，然后就能处理好。

sentences.en: This is like a weird skill that I have a couple of friends with ADHD that they just seem to be able to do, where it's like everyone else is freaking out.
sentences.zh: 这可能再次归因于对解离的高度依赖。

sentences.en: And normally I would assume that they would be having the same, if not a more emotional reaction and they just become like hyper-focused and they can just deal with it.
sentences.zh: 大脑可以在这些时刻利用它来获得优势。

sentences.en: This may be, again, because of this high reliance on dissociation.
sentences.zh: 当然，解离与焦虑、抑郁和其他情绪障碍之间也存在联系，

sentences.en: The brain can use it to its advantage during these moments.
sentences.zh: 但这里最大的风险因素——如果你在学术场合或满是心理学家的房间里提到解离，每个人都会跟你谈论的那个因素——就是创伤。

sentences.en: There is also, of course, a link between dissociation and anxiety and depression and other mood
sentences.zh: 创伤是研究人员在提到解离时会为你引用的最重要的因素。

sentences.en: disorders, but the biggest risk factor here, like the one that everyone is going to talk
sentences.zh: 最近有一份报告显示，经历过创伤的人群中，解离的发生率比普通人高出近60%到70%。

sentences.en: to you about if you mention dissociation in an academic room or in a room full of psychologists is trauma.
sentences.zh: 这是过去50年心理学研究中重复验证次数最多的发现之一。

sentences.en: Trauma is the biggest thing that researchers will cite for you when it comes to dissociation.
sentences.zh: 创伤和解离就像是一对形影不离的伙伴。

sentences.en: There was a recent report that suggests that the rates of dissociation are almost 60% to 70% higher in people who have experienced trauma than the average individual.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我们最近在播客里谈论了很多关于创伤的话题。

sentences.en: That is one of the most replicated findings you will find from the last 50 years in psychology.
sentences.zh: 以及作为人类的艰难之处，以及我们的大脑和身体对此做出的反应。

sentences.en: Trauma and dissociation are like two Ps in a pod.
sentences.zh: 这在过去几个月里一直是我们讨论的一个共同主题。

sentences.en: I feel like we've been talking about trauma a lot on the podcast recently.
sentences.zh: 我不知道你有没有注意到，但我认为这是因为你对这些主题的文献研究得越深，

sentences.en: And just the hard parts of being human and how our brain and our bodies respond to that.
sentences.zh: 你就越会意识到我们被负面经历塑造得有多深，

sentences.en: It's been like a common theme for us in the last couple of months.
sentences.zh: 以及身体是如何本能地保留这些经历的——无论好坏——

sentences.en: I don't know if you've noticed, but I think it's because the deeper you get into the literature
sentences.zh: 并以某种方式最终塑造了我们的个性和我们对事物的反应，而我们甚至对此一无所知。

sentences.en: on these topics, the more you kind of realize how deeply shaped we are by the negative experiences
sentences.zh: 情感虐待、忽视、不一致的照料，还有童年霸凌、经历自然灾害、经历父母离婚。

sentences.en: that we may have and how the body instinctively holds onto these experiences for better or for worse
sentences.zh: 当然，这些都可能为以后生活中的解离埋下伏笔。

sentences.en: in ways that do end up shaping our personality and how we respond to things without even knowing.
sentences.zh: 所以有一个理论叫做结构性解离理论，它解释了原因。

sentences.en: Emotional abuse, neglect, inconsistent caregiving, but also childhood bullying, surviving a natural disaster, surviving your parents' divorce.
sentences.zh: 根据这个模型，当一个孩子经历反复的压倒性压力时，比如听到父母不断争吵、受到照料者的威胁、

sentences.en: Of course, that can create a blueprint for dissociation later on in life.
sentences.zh: 每天在学校待七到八个小时，感觉需要躲藏，或者必须时刻提防，或者总是感到格格不入。

sentences.en: So there is this theory called the structural dissociation theory that explains why.
sentences.zh: 他们的人格实际上可以分裂成我们所说的“表象正常部分”（ANPs），这是他们用来处理日常生活的；

sentences.en: According to this model, when a child experiences repeated overwhelming stress, you know, hearing their parents constantly fighting, being threatened by a caregiver,
sentences.zh: 以及“情感部分”（EPs），这是他们储存未处理创伤的部分。

sentences.en: being at school seven to eight hours a day and feeling like they need to hide or, you know, have to look over their shoulder or are just constantly feeling out of place.
sentences.zh: 这个系统学会了在这些部分之间切换，作为一种生存策略。

sentences.en: Their personality can actually split into what we call apparently normal parts or ANPs, which is what they use to handle daily life.
sentences.zh: 在学校或与父母在一起时，表象正常部分（ANPs）会表现出来。

sentences.en: And then emotional parts, EPs, which are the parts of them that store the unprocessed trauma.
sentences.zh: 但随后还有那些被隐藏起来的情感部分，他们只是偶尔触碰一下，

sentences.en: The system learns to switch between these parts as a survival strategy.
sentences.zh: 他们其实并不想触碰，他们的大脑也不想触碰，但它依然存在。

sentences.en: At school, you know, with a parent, the apparently normal parts, the ANPs, will be on display.
sentences.zh: 在实践中，这意味着即使作为成年人，有这种经历的人在生活中遇到呼应原始创伤的触发点时，也会经历解离。

sentences.en: But then there are these emotional parts that are hidden away that they only briefly kind of dip into,
sentences.zh: 一个大嗓门、一种威胁的语气、一个感到无力的处境，甚至像人际关系困难或冲突，都会让人觉得：我知道该怎么处理这个。

sentences.en: that they don't really want to touch, their brain doesn't really want to touch, but is still there.
sentences.zh: 我只要戴上这个面具就行了。

sentences.en: In practice, this means that even as adults, people with this kind of history can experience dissociation when a trigger comes into their life that echoes the original trauma.
sentences.zh: 我只要从这里淡出，在这个状态下，我是安全的。

sentences.en: A loud voice, a threatening tone, a situation where they feel powerless, even like relationship difficulties or conflict can cause people to be like, I know how to deal with this.
sentences.zh: 即使我感觉非常奇怪。

sentences.en: I'll just slip this mask on.
sentences.zh: 并不是说现在客观上很危险。

sentences.en: I'll just fade out of this and here in this state, I can be safe.
sentences.zh: 只是神经系统再次识别出了类似于过去创伤的环境线索。

sentences.en: Even if I feel completely weird.
sentences.zh: 而这些来自早年生活的模式将我们切换到了保护模式，因为你的身体还能做什么呢？

sentences.en: It's not that the present is objectively dangerous.
sentences.zh: 难道要忽视它认为即将发生的危险吗？

sentences.en: It's just that the nervous system, again, recognizes an environmental cue that resembles past trauma.
sentences.zh: 那不是它的程序设定。

sentences.en: And these patterns from early life switch us into protective mode because what else is your body going to do?
sentences.zh: 这就是解离变得非常适应不良的地方。

sentences.en: Just ignore when it thinks something dangerous is about to happen?
sentences.zh: 当它对那些不再存在的威胁做出反应，或者当它成为我们大脑在遇到可怕事情时唯一会回到的策略时。

sentences.en: That's not its programming.
sentences.zh: 而此时其实有更好的选择可用。

sentences.en: This is where dissociation can become really maladaptive.
sentences.zh: 如果你的大脑再次学习到早年的世界是危险的，

sentences.en: When it's responding to threats that aren't there anymore or when it becomes the only strategy that our brain keeps going back to when things are scary.
sentences.zh: 而继续生存下去的唯一方法就是将大部分经历离线，或者漂浮在世界之上，或者漂浮在自己之上。

sentences.en: And when better options are available for it.
sentences.zh: 那些解离模式就会变得稳固下来。

sentences.en: If your brain, again,
sentences.zh: 如果你的大脑再次

sentences.en: learns that the early world is dangerous and the only way to keep going through this is to put large parts of that experience offline or to kind of float above the world or float above yourself.
sentences.zh: 学习到早年的世界是危险的，而继续生存下去的唯一方法就是将大部分经历离线，或者漂浮在世界之上，或者漂浮在自己之上。

sentences.en: Those dissociative patterns can become stabilised.
sentences.zh: 那些解离模式就会变得稳固下来。

sentences.en: I was actually reading up on a bunch of cases about this in a couple of psychiatric journals just to see how this presents.
sentences.zh: 我最近其实在几本精神病学期刊上读到过很多关于这方面的案例，就是想看看这种症状是如何表现的。

sentences.en: And there was one case.
sentences.zh: 其中有一个案例。

sentences.en: Actually, there's a couple of cases I'll read to you that were super interesting.
sentences.zh: 其实，我有几个案例想读给你听，它们都超级有趣。

sentences.en: The first was of a young 21-year-old guy and he experienced a really bad dissociative episode when he got back in touch with his estranged father.
sentences.zh: 第一个案例是一名21岁的年轻人，他在与疏远已久的父亲重新取得联系时，经历了一次非常严重的解离发作。

sentences.en: And he dissociated for, I think it was like three or four days.
sentences.zh: 我想他解离了大约三到四天。

sentences.en: He couldn't remember being admitted into a psychiatric hospital.
sentences.zh: 他不记得自己是如何被送进精神病院的。

sentences.en: He couldn't remember anything that had happened to him in the last three to four days of his life, despite being really, really healthy and otherwise completely fine.
sentences.zh: 他不记得过去三四天里发生在他身上的任何事情，尽管他平时非常非常健康，其他方面也完全正常。

sentences.en: And afterwards, he told physicians that the last time this had happened to him was, surprise, surprise, when he was a young kid and he'd last seen his father.
sentences.zh: 事后，他告诉医生，上一次发生这种情况时，不出所料，还是在他小时候最后一次见到他父亲的时候。

sentences.en: You know, it'd been years, I think for him, and maybe it'd even been over a decade since he'd seen his father.
sentences.zh: 你知道，对他来说已经过去好几年了，我想甚至可能超过十年没见过他父亲了。

sentences.en: And yet he was right back there.
sentences.zh: 然而，他却瞬间回到了那种状态。

sentences.en: And this ancient part of our brain is like, OK, I know what to do here.
sentences.zh: 我们大脑中这个古老的部分就像是在说：好吧，我知道这里该怎么做。

sentences.en: Another case I read was someone in their 50s who reported that at 24,
sentences.zh: 我读到的另一个案例是一位50多岁的人，她报告说在24岁时，

sentences.en: it was like her life suddenly changed color and she felt like everything became dampened after a serious traumatic event.
sentences.zh: 那感觉就像是她的人生突然变了色，在经历了一次严重的创伤事件后，她觉得一切都变得暗淡了。

sentences.en: And since then, she'd only had a few moments every year when she had felt normal.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，她每年只有那么几个瞬间会感到正常。

sentences.en: But she actually was telling physicians that like she liked how she felt.
sentences.zh: 但她实际上告诉医生，她其实挺喜欢这种感觉的。

sentences.en: She was like, I don't, I know it's a problem.
sentences.zh: 她说：我不知道，我知道这是一个问题。

sentences.en: My family tells me it's a problem.
sentences.zh: 我的家人也告诉我这是一个问题。

sentences.en: But I like this feeling of sometimes not feeling real or not feeling like the world is real or detaching myself from what's going on around me.
sentences.zh: 但我喜欢这种感觉，有时感觉不真实，或者觉得世界不真实，又或者把自己从周围发生的事情中抽离出来。

sentences.en: It just feels more peaceful.
sentences.zh: 这感觉更平静。

sentences.en: Again, a maladaptive coping strategy.
sentences.zh: 再说一次，这是一种适应不良的应对策略。

sentences.en: It's probably about time we bring up dissociative identity disorder and what we previously knew as multiple personality disorder.
sentences.zh: 现在大概是我们谈谈解离性身份障碍（以前被称为多重人格障碍）的时候了。

sentences.en: Because when trauma is really extreme, there is this thing that can happen,
sentences.zh: 因为当创伤达到极端程度时，确实会发生这种情况，

sentences.en: this phenomena where someone's personality splits so deeply that they feel like they are different people at different times.
sentences.zh: 这种现象就是某人的性格分裂得如此之深，以至于他们觉得自己在不同时间是不同的人。

sentences.en: Now, this is not everyday dissociation.
sentences.zh: 这可不是日常的解离。

sentences.en: This is not feeling unreal and panicked by that feeling.
sentences.zh: 这也不是那种因为感到不真实而产生的恐慌。

sentences.en: This is when children especially go through such a terrible thing in their life that the only way they endure it is to say,
sentences.zh: 这是当孩子们，尤其是当孩子们在生活中经历了如此可怕的事情，以至于他们唯一的忍受方式就是说，

sentences.en: is to almost create an alter or a persona that it's happening to that is not them as a way to protect their ego.
sentences.zh: 就是几乎创造出一个替身或人格来承受这一切，而那个替身不是他们自己，以此来保护他们的自我。

sentences.en: And those people, once they are created in their mind, it's very hard to kill them.
sentences.zh: 而这些人，一旦在他们的脑海中被创造出来，就很难消灭他们。

sentences.en: Some people even have amnesia about this.
sentences.zh: 有些人甚至对此有失忆症。

sentences.en: There's an incredible YouTube video that I think you should watch titled, oh, okay, I need to remember.
sentences.zh: 有一个很棒的YouTube视频，我觉得你应该看看，标题是，哦，好吧，我得记一下。

sentences.en: I think it's titled, Living with 12 Alternative Personalities for 60 Years.
sentences.zh: 我想标题是《与12个人格共存60年》。

sentences.en: And it interviews a woman called Amanda who has 12 alters.
sentences.zh: 视频采访了一位名叫阿曼达的女性，她有12个人格。

sentences.en: 12 different personalities that have emerged from and through traumatic periods in her life.
sentences.zh: 这12种不同的人格都是在她生命中经历创伤时期时产生的。

sentences.en: Some of them are children, some of them are teenagers, some of them are men, some of them are women, some of them are older.
sentences.zh: 其中一些是孩子，一些是青少年，一些是男性，一些是女性，还有一些是长者。

sentences.en: And she switches between them sometimes on a daily, sometimes monthly.
sentences.zh: 她有时每天，有时每月在这些人格之间切换。

sentences.en: They feel like she's like, when I am in this person, I am this person.
sentences.zh: 他们感觉就像是，她说：当我处于这个人格时，我就是这个人。

sentences.en: I don't have amnesia about it.
sentences.zh: 我对此并没有失忆。

sentences.en: The way she tries to explain it is like someone trying to explain colors that don't exiSt.
sentences.zh: 她试图解释的方式就像有人试图解释不存在的颜色一样。

sentences.en: Like you just probably can't see it or understand it unless you are her.
sentences.zh: 就像你除非是她，否则可能根本无法看到或理解它。

sentences.en: And she describes the first time she experienced this as a child when something horrible happened to her.
sentences.zh: 她描述了她小时候第一次经历这种情况，当时发生了一些可怕的事情。

sentences.en: And she, again, was like, this is not happening to me.
sentences.zh: 她当时又说：这不是发生在我身上。

sentences.en: This is happening to Jenny.
sentences.zh: 这是发生在珍妮身上。

sentences.en: Hi, Jenny.
sentences.zh: 你好，珍妮。

sentences.en: And then Jenny was this part of her personality that dissociated and broke off.
sentences.zh: 然后珍妮就是她性格中解离并分裂出去的那一部分。

sentences.en: And she just kept relying on the strategy and kept splitting until she is the person she is today.
sentences.zh: 她就一直依赖这种策略，不断分裂，直到成为今天的她。

sentences.en: What's so interesting and what I found so interesting about this video was she was like, they all have different opinions.
sentences.zh: 最有趣的是，我发现这个视频最有趣的地方在于她说：他们都有不同的观点。

sentences.en: They kind of have different voices.
sentences.zh: 他们有不同的声音。

sentences.en: They have different even political beliefs, different food preferences.
sentences.zh: 他们甚至有不同的政治信仰，不同的食物偏好。

sentences.en: And she even in this interview like switches between her and I think the guy like one of her personalities called Bradley like on camera.
sentences.zh: 在这次采访中，她甚至在镜头前在自己和我想是她其中一个人格叫布拉德利之间切换。

sentences.en: And the reason I bring this extreme case up is because firstly, I think it's important to see the level, like the maximum level at which this can develop to.
sentences.zh: 我提出这个极端案例的原因是，首先，我认为看到这种症状发展的最高程度是很重要的。

sentences.en: It's almost comforting to know that like even if that was where I ended up or you ended up, like you would still be okay.
sentences.zh: 知道即使那是我的终点，或者你的终点，你依然会没事的，这几乎是一种安慰。

sentences.en: This woman seems actually very happy and very loved.
sentences.zh: 这个女人看起来其实非常快乐，也非常被爱。

sentences.en: But also because in those unique cases, you really can see the anatomy of this mechanism.
sentences.zh: 但也是因为在这些独特的案例中，你真的可以看到这种机制的解剖结构。

sentences.en: You can see exactly more clearly, I guess, what is happening to you.
sentences.zh: 我想你可以更清楚地看到，到底发生了什么。

sentences.en: You are obviously not splitting into a different personality, but it's the same premise.
sentences.zh: 你显然不会分裂成不同的人格，但前提是一样的。

sentences.en: Your brain just needs a break.
sentences.zh: 你的大脑只是需要休息一下。

sentences.en: It just needs to clock out for a little bit.
sentences.zh: 它只是需要暂时下班一会儿。

sentences.en: I will say it's very unlikely that this will happen to you, especially if you are over the age of 12.
sentences.zh: 我要说的是，这种情况不太可能发生在你身上，尤其是如果你已经超过12岁的话。

sentences.en: You have to have experienced intense trauma in your childhood to be diagnosed with dissociative identity disorder.
sentences.zh: 你必须在童年时期经历过严重的创伤才会被诊断为解离性身份障碍。

sentences.en: Obviously, some people get diagnosed later in life.
sentences.zh: 当然，有些人是在以后的生活中才被诊断出来的。

sentences.en: But I think it's important to realize that these really intense cases are super rare.
sentences.zh: 但我认为重要的是要意识到，这些非常极端的案例是超级罕见的。

sentences.en: So if you are experiencing everyday dissociation, yes, it's really scary, but you're probably not going to end up in this extreme state.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你正在经历日常的解离，是的，这真的很可怕，但你很可能不会陷入这种极端状态。

sentences.en: And even if you do, you will survive.
sentences.zh: 即使你真的陷入了，你也会活下来的。

sentences.en: You may have relied on dissociation for a long time without realizing it.
sentences.zh: 你可能在没有意识到的情况下长期依赖解离。

sentences.en: It doesn't mean that you're always going to feel this way or be in this state.
sentences.zh: 这并不意味着你永远都会有这种感觉或处于这种状态。

sentences.en: The good news is that your nervous system is completely plastic.
sentences.zh: 好消息是你的神经系统是完全可塑的。

sentences.en: It is changeable.
sentences.zh: 它是可以改变的。

sentences.en: Therefore, there is a way to switch off chronic dissociative responses and to really feel more in touch with reality and the feeling of being real and the feeling of being alive.
sentences.zh: 因此，有一种方法可以关闭慢性的解离反应，真正地感受到与现实的联系，感受到真实感和活着的感觉。

sentences.en: Even if maybe that is in itself equally confronting, it's good to know the possibility is there and that you can remove this filter over your experiences.
sentences.zh: 即使这本身可能同样令人难以面对，但知道这种可能性存在，并且你可以移除覆盖在你体验上的这层滤镜，是一件好事。

sentences.en: And that's what we're going to talk about next.

sentences.en: In true psychology of your 20s fashion, I want to give you some strategies that might help if you have noticed in yourself that you have a tendency to not feel real,
sentences.zh: 以《二十岁心理学》的风格，我想给你一些策略，如果你发现自己有不真实感，

sentences.en: to not feel like the world is real or to dissociate.
sentences.zh: 觉得世界不真实或者有解离倾向，这些策略可能会有所帮助。

sentences.en: Like I said, this is something that I experience quite a bit, especially when I'm sleep deprived, especially when I'm stressed, especially when I have a lot on my plate.
sentences.zh: 就像我说的那样，我经常经历这种情况，尤其是在睡眠不足、压力大或者手头事情很多的时候。

sentences.en: I often find that I will have these like really scary moments right before I go to bed where automatically my brain is like, oh, well,
sentences.zh: 我经常发现，就在我睡觉前，我会经历这些非常可怕的时刻，我的大脑会自动说：哦，好吧，

sentences.en: did you know that you're not actually real and that you're not actually here?
sentences.zh: 你知道你其实并不真实，你其实并不在这里吗？

sentences.en: And I'm like, can we, can we cut with, can we not with that?
sentences.zh: 我就说：我们能，我们能停止吗，我们能别这样吗？

sentences.en: Like I'm sick of feeling this way.
sentences.zh: 我受够了这种感觉。

sentences.en: Like let's, let's cut the cameras on that one.
sentences.zh: 我们把那个念头掐断吧。

sentences.en: But I have actually discovered some really helpful strategies that like make me the boss of that feeling and immediately kind of shut it up to be like the most polite about it.
sentences.zh: 但我确实发现了一些非常有用的策略，让我能掌控那种感觉，并立即让它闭嘴，用最礼貌的方式来说。

sentences.en: You know, a lot of people talk about grounding, you know, naming five things that you can see, hear, feel, maybe even taste, placing your feet on the grass, in the dirt,
sentences.zh: 你知道，很多人谈论接地气，你知道，列出你能看到、听到、感觉到，甚至可能尝到的五样东西，把脚放在草地上、泥土里、

sentences.en: in the sand and really connecting with, with the earth.
sentences.zh: 沙子里，真正地与大地连接。

sentences.en: Um, those are all great strategies, probably ones that we know, and sometimes it just doesn't cut it.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这些都是很好的策略，可能我们都知道，但有时它们就是不管用。

sentences.en: So here are some things that might take this to the next level for you and might actively be able to pull you back into the world when dissociation hits.
sentences.zh: 所以这里有一些东西可能会让你更上一层楼，当解离来袭时，可能能够主动把你拉回这个世界。

sentences.en: The first being safety scaffolding.
sentences.zh: 第一是安全脚手架。

sentences.en: If dissociation happens, it really helps to have a predictable low effort ritual that signals safety to your nervous system.
sentences.zh: 如果发生了解离，拥有一个可预测的、低努力的仪式来向你的神经系统发出安全信号，真的很有帮助。

sentences.en: That could be a short recorded audio that you've made of your own voice saying a really calming mantra or just saying, hey, I know you're not feeling real right now.
sentences.zh: 那可以是一段你自己录制的短音频，用你自己的声音说一段非常平静的咒语，或者只是说：嘿，我知道你现在感觉不真实。

sentences.en: I can promise you, you definitely are.
sentences.zh: 我可以向你保证，你绝对是真实的。

sentences.en: It could also be the voice of someone else, like a meditation that you always come back to.
sentences.zh: 它也可以是别人的声音，比如你总是会听的冥想音频。

sentences.en: So the familiarity of the voice, whether it's your own or a voice that you listen to a lot, reduces the initial alarm state that you might be feeling because it signals, okay,
sentences.zh: 所以声音的熟悉感，无论是你自己的还是你经常听的声音，都能减少你可能感到的最初的警报状态，因为它发出了信号：好吧，

sentences.en: something I know well and something I know to be true is here.
sentences.zh: 我熟悉的东西和我知道是真实的东西就在这里。

sentences.en: I must be present because this is something that I keep coming back to.
sentences.zh: 我一定是在场的，因为这是我不断回到的东西。

sentences.en: This is something that has been continuous.
sentences.zh: 这是持续存在的东西。

sentences.en: This mantra for myself, this meditation has always been here through these moments.
sentences.zh: 这个我自己的咒语，这个冥想，在这些时刻一直都在这里。

sentences.en: It's just like having an anchor to hold on to.
sentences.zh: 这就像有一个可以抓住的锚。

sentences.en: Another kind of scaffolding is anything sensory.
sentences.zh: 另一种脚手架是任何感官上的东西。

sentences.en: A Rubik's cube, a mint lozenge, chewing gum, something like that.
sentences.zh: 魔方、薄荷糖、口香糖，诸如此类的东西。

sentences.en: I've also given this tip before.
sentences.zh: 我也给过这个建议。

sentences.en: Warheads, sour candies have been a lifesaver for me in these moments because the extreme sensory experience of this candy,
sentences.zh: Warheads酸糖在这些时刻简直是我的救命稻草，因为这种糖带来的极端感官体验，

sentences.en: it like genuinely shocks me and brings me back into the present because it's something that I cannot ignore.
sentences.zh: 它真的震撼了我，把我带回了现在，因为这是我无法忽视的东西。

sentences.en: It is this like real thing that is like,
sentences.zh: 它是这种真实的东西，就像是，

sentences.en: of course you're alive because how could I be alive and be experiencing or not be alive and be experiencing this like so intensely and it's just like the shock that just like catapults me right back to where my feet are planted.
sentences.zh: 你当然活着，因为如果我不活着，怎么可能经历这一切，或者如果不活着，怎么可能经历得如此强烈？这就像是一种震撼，直接把我弹回我双脚站立的地方。

sentences.en: I think it's also like a distraction technique.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这也可以算是一种分心技巧。

sentences.en: Like when you're chewing or licking or whatever, consuming something that's that sour,
sentences.zh: 就像当你咀嚼或舔舐，或者无论怎样，消费某种那么酸的东西时，

sentences.en: sometimes you just like can't really think about anything else and it lets you just for a moment stop thinking about thinking about not being real or the world not being real,
sentences.zh: 有时你就是无法思考其他任何事情，它让你暂时停止思考关于不真实，或者世界不真实的事情，

sentences.en: if you know what I mean.
sentences.zh: 如果你明白我的意思的话。

sentences.en: I know as well that when I'm flying overseas, I will or flying anywhere, like I will feel a sense of derealization a lot more.
sentences.zh: 我也知道，当我在海外飞行时，或者飞往任何地方时，我会感到更多的现实解体感。

sentences.en: So I also always bring something from home, like a little figurine from my house on every trip that I just like set in my hotel room or like bring with me in my bag.
sentences.zh: 所以我每次旅行总是带一些家里的东西，比如家里的小摆件，我把它放在酒店房间里，或者随身带在包里。

sentences.en: And it has this weird therapeutic effect on me, I don't know what it is, but again,
sentences.zh: 它对我有一种奇怪的治疗效果，我不知道为什么，但再说一次，

sentences.en: like I think especially being away from my environment that I love and that I cherish and like from my dog and like from my life, I can feel quite unstable.
sentences.zh: 我觉得尤其是离开了我所爱和珍惜的环境，离开我的狗，离开我的生活，我会感到相当不稳定。

sentences.en: And having this like really otherwise quite silly,
sentences.zh: 而带着这个本来相当愚蠢的、

sentences.en: stupid thing that would otherwise just be like this ornamental thing in my house with me on this trip pulls me back to that environment where I feel my safeSt.
sentences.zh: 无聊的东西，如果不是这次旅行，它可能只是我家里的装饰品，它把我拉回了那个我感到最安全的环境。

sentences.en: I've also heard of someone, a friend of mine who brings a sheet of stickers with her everywhere she goes and anytime she feels strange or she feels odd,
sentences.zh: 我也听说过一个人，我的一个朋友，她去哪里都带着一叠贴纸，每当她感到奇怪或不对劲时，

sentences.en: she will pull out a sticker and it's like one of those 3D stickers, like those squishy ones.
sentences.zh: 她就会拿出一张贴纸，就像那种3D贴纸，那种软绵绵的。

sentences.en: And she will like stick one onto the wall or her computer or a mirror or like the back of the bus seat and just like focus on it.
sentences.zh: 她会把一张贴在墙上、电脑上、镜子上，或者公交车座椅后面，然后专注于它。

sentences.en: And she's like, oh, well, I'm bringing like, at least this thing is real.
sentences.zh: 她说：哦，好吧，我至少带着，至少这个东西是真的。

sentences.en: At least I have these stickers that I'm bringing with me and to every single different situation.
sentences.zh: 至少我有这些贴纸，我带着它们去每一个不同的地方。

sentences.en: And I know it sounds silly, but sometimes for something is like extreme and scary as derealization,
sentences.zh: 我知道这听起来很傻，但有时对于像现实解体这样极端和可怕的事情，

sentences.en: you just have to either beat it with complete reason or beat it with silliness and being a little bit goofy with it and like playing with the feeling.
sentences.zh: 你只能要么用完全的理性去战胜它，要么用愚蠢去战胜它，带点傻气，玩弄这种感觉。

sentences.en: These are all kind of sensory or physical anchors.
sentences.zh: 这些都是感官或物理上的锚。

sentences.en: We can also use kinesthetic anchors, which is basically just a fancy word for moving your body like and really moving it.
sentences.zh: 我们也可以使用动觉锚，这基本上只是移动身体的华丽说法，而且是真正地移动它。

sentences.en: Don't just like look at your hands and feet as they like wriggle.
sentences.zh: 不要只是看着你的手脚扭动。

sentences.en: That can still feel kind of disorientating.
sentences.zh: 那仍然会让人感到有点迷失方向。

sentences.en: I want you to like fully, rapidly, violently shake your whole body.
sentences.zh: 我希望你能够充分、快速、剧烈地摇晃你的整个身体。

sentences.en: Dance, stretch, move, run, just like spasm in the air.
sentences.zh: 跳舞、伸展、移动、奔跑，就像在空中痉挛一样。

sentences.en: Do something that you feel reconnects you with your limbs and your fingers and your toenails.
sentences.zh: 做一些你觉得能让你重新连接四肢、手指和脚趾的事情。

sentences.en: A 2014 study that I particularly love explored how dance therapy specifically helps people exit dissociation when other things aren't working.
sentences.zh: 我特别喜欢的一项2014年的研究探讨了舞蹈疗法如何专门帮助人们在其他方法无效时走出解离状态。

sentences.en: Because it creates kinesthetic awareness.
sentences.zh: 因为它能建立动觉意识。

sentences.en: And this is our body's natural ability to detect and locate and recognize our body, our form in space and time and our surroundings.
sentences.zh: 这是我们身体的一种本能，能感知、定位并识别我们的身体、我们在时空中的形态以及我们周围的环境。

sentences.en: And that kinesthetic awareness really activates something mentally within us as well that obviously recognizes that we must be present to be having this feeling.
sentences.zh: 这种动觉意识在心理层面也激活了一些东西，让我们清楚地意识到，为了产生这种感觉，我们必须身处当下。

sentences.en: And so it brings us back to our sense of realness.
sentences.zh: 所以它把我们带回了对真实感的认知。

sentences.en: Even like repetitive, rhythmic movements like bouncing your knee or rolling your shoulders or flowing, moving your body have been shown to provide that same grounding experience.
sentences.zh: 即使是一些重复的、有节奏的动作，比如抖腿、转动肩膀或舒展身体，也被证明能提供同样的接地感。

sentences.en: It positions you back in the room.
sentences.zh: 它能让你重新回到当下的空间里。

sentences.en: It shows you that you are in control, that you can feel time and space and movement around you.
sentences.zh: 它向你证明你掌控着一切，你能感受到周围的时间、空间和运动。

sentences.en: It also helps you obviously release tension.
sentences.zh: 它显然也有助于你释放压力。

sentences.en: We know that stress is like a big trigger for dissociation.
sentences.zh: 我们知道压力是导致解离的一个重要诱因。

sentences.en: And sometimes that might also be why this mechanism works.
sentences.zh: 有时这可能就是这种机制起作用的原因。

sentences.en: I will also say, sometimes you don't want to think even more about the feeling.
sentences.zh: 我还要说，有时候你并不想对这种感觉想得太多。

sentences.en: But it's kind of liberating to argue with it.
sentences.zh: 但与这种感觉进行辩论其实是一种解脱。

sentences.en: To argue with the I'm not real, I'm not here thought.
sentences.zh: 去反驳“我不真实”、“我不在这里”这种想法。

sentences.en: If your mind is saying that I'm not real, this isn't real, whatever it is, this may sound counterintuitive, but I think about how liberating that maybe would be if that was true.
sentences.zh: 如果你的大脑在说“我不真实”、“这不真实”之类的，这听起来可能有点反直觉，但我会想，如果这是真的，那该多解脱啊。

sentences.en: Like I know that this thought is scary to me, but I argue with the thought and I think, but what if that was a good thing?
sentences.zh: 我知道这个想法让我害怕，但我会反驳它，我会想，如果这是件好事呢？

sentences.en: Let me explain, like if I wasn't real, it meant that something would have to be controlling this experience.
sentences.zh: 让我解释一下，如果我不真实，那就意味着有什么东西在操控这一切。

sentences.en: And that makes me feel assured in the idea that something is out there that is bigger than us.
sentences.zh: 这让我感到安心，因为我相信有什么比我们更宏大的存在。

sentences.en: And that's actually deeply comforting.
sentences.zh: 这其实是非常令人慰藉的。

sentences.en: And it's like you were trying to scare me with this feeling.
sentences.zh: 就好像你想用这种感觉来吓唬我一样。

sentences.en: Actually, a part of it might be deeply like existentially validating or, you know, another thought that we have, like I'm not actually here.
sentences.zh: 实际上，其中一部分可能在存在主义层面上非常有意义，或者，你知道，我们还有另一种想法，比如“我其实不在这里”。

sentences.en: Well, then that's fucking great.
sentences.zh: 好吧，那真是太棒了。

sentences.en: That eliminates a lot of my social anxiety, doesn't it?
sentences.zh: 这消除了我很多社交焦虑，不是吗？

sentences.en: Why am I so worried about being perceived if I'm not even real, if the perception of me isn't even happening?
sentences.zh: 如果我根本不真实，如果对我的感知甚至都没有发生，那我为什么还要担心被别人注视呢？

sentences.en: Sometimes that's just like helpful to like turn off the anxiousness tap before I come back down and realize like firstly that this feeling is quite silly and to challenge it.
sentences.zh: 有时候，在冷静下来并意识到这种感觉很荒谬、需要去挑战它之前，这种想法能帮我关掉焦虑的阀门。

sentences.en: But also to say that like even if this was the case, is that even a bad thing?
sentences.zh: 但也要说，即使真是这样，这又有什么不好呢？

sentences.en: Because my anxiety and my panic that is rising in response to my depersonalization or my derealization is only rising because it is perceiving it as a terrible, terrifying thing.
sentences.zh: 因为我因人格解体或现实解体而产生的焦虑和恐慌，之所以会上升，仅仅是因为它把这视为一件可怕、恐怖的事情。

sentences.en: What if it wasn't?
sentences.zh: 如果它不是呢？

sentences.en: These are actually, they have a name.
sentences.zh: 这些其实是有名字的。

sentences.en: They're called cognitive scripts.
sentences.zh: 它们被称为认知脚本。

sentences.en: They have been proven to help with this feeling.
sentences.zh: 事实证明它们有助于缓解这种感觉。

sentences.en: Another really famous one that you've probably heard comes from the philosopher René Descartes, which says, I think therefore I am.
sentences.zh: 另一个你可能听说过的非常著名的例子来自哲学家勒内·笛卡尔，他说：“我思故我在”。

sentences.en: Also a Billie Eilish song.
sentences.zh: 这也是碧梨的一首歌。

sentences.en: Basically, this phrase, this mantra, I think therefore I am, tells us that the very act of doubting your own existence actually proves that you exiSt.
sentences.zh: 基本上，这句话，这个咒语，“我思故我在”，告诉我们，怀疑自身存在这一行为本身，恰恰证明了你的存在。

sentences.en: How?
sentences.zh: 怎么证明？

sentences.en: Because to doubt, you have to be thinking.
sentences.zh: 因为要怀疑，你就必须在思考。

sentences.en: And thinking is something that only a conscious mind can do.
sentences.zh: 而思考是只有清醒的头脑才能做到的事。

sentences.en: The very act of questioning, am I real?
sentences.zh: 质疑“我真实吗？”这一行为本身，

sentences.en: Is this real?
sentences.zh: “这真实吗？”

sentences.en: Is proof that you are.
sentences.zh: 就是你存在的证明。

sentences.en: And I know this feels a little bit meta, but that's the reassuring part.
sentences.zh: 我知道这听起来有点元认知，但这正是令人安心的部分。

sentences.en: The fact that you are noticing that you are dissociating, that you are questioning reality, that is all proof that you must be existing in order to have those thoughts.
sentences.zh: 你注意到自己在解离、在质疑现实，这一切都证明了你必须存在才能产生这些想法。

sentences.en: Even when it feels like the world is fuzzy or your awareness isn't in itself a solid anchor, this in itself is like something we can always come back to.
sentences.zh: 即使当世界感觉模糊，或者你的意识本身不是一个坚实的锚点时，这本身就是我们可以随时回归的东西。

sentences.en: It's this subtle cognitive reminder that you may feel disconnected.
sentences.zh: 这是一种微妙的认知提醒，提醒你虽然可能感到脱节，

sentences.en: That's just your individual experience.
sentences.zh: 那只是你个人的体验。

sentences.en: It doesn't mean that reality itself or the world around you has disappeared.
sentences.zh: 这并不意味着现实本身或你周围的世界已经消失了。

sentences.en: It's just a natural response to stress.
sentences.zh: 这只是对压力的一种自然反应。

sentences.en: It's a natural response to perhaps trauma in your past, but even just not getting enough sleep.
sentences.zh: 这是对过去创伤的一种自然反应，甚至仅仅是因为睡眠不足。

sentences.en: Even just having a really hard day.
sentences.zh: 甚至只是因为度过了非常艰难的一天。

sentences.en: I want to again remind you, this whole process of feeling like everything is kind of blurring out or fuzzy or not real.
sentences.zh: 我想再次提醒你，这种感觉一切都在模糊、虚幻或不真实的过程，

sentences.en: Is your brain trying to just give you a bit of a break and cut you some slack?
sentences.zh: 只是你的大脑在试图让你休息一下，对你宽容一点。

sentences.en: It definitely doesn't feel nice.
sentences.zh: 这绝对不是什么好受的感觉。

sentences.en: It doesn't mean that it's wrong.
sentences.zh: 但这并不意味着它是错的。

sentences.en: And it doesn't mean that something is wrong with you.
sentences.zh: 也不意味着你出了什么问题。

sentences.en: Or that something is, this is an indicator of something dangerous that's going to happen to you.
sentences.zh: 或者这预示着什么危险的事情即将发生在你身上。

sentences.en: I think this is a gentle reminder that this is a human process.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一个温和的提醒，提醒你这是一个人类都会经历的过程。

sentences.en: This is just noise.
sentences.zh: 这只是噪音。

sentences.en: Your brain isn't betraying you.
sentences.zh: 你的大脑并没有背叛你。

sentences.en: It's not trying to tell you something.
sentences.zh: 它不是在试图告诉你什么。

sentences.en: It's just trying to help you survive.
sentences.zh: 它只是在试图帮你生存下去。

sentences.en: You are real.
sentences.zh: 你是真实的。

sentences.en: You are here.
sentences.zh: 你就在这里。

sentences.en: I promise you that.
sentences.zh: 我向你保证。

sentences.en: You are listening to my voice.
sentences.zh: 你正在听我的声音。

sentences.en: In your ears right now.
sentences.zh: 就在你的耳朵里。

sentences.en: That is confirmation.
sentences.zh: 这就是确认。

sentences.en: And you're going to survive this.
sentences.zh: 你会挺过这一关的。

sentences.en: You're going to survive this overwhelm.
sentences.zh: 你会挺过这种不知所措的感觉的。

sentences.en: I know it can feel super unpleasant.
sentences.zh: 我知道这感觉非常不愉快。

sentences.en: But everyone who has been through this, which is, if the estimates say, nearly every person on this planet has come through on the other side.
sentences.zh: 但每一个经历过这些的人——据估计，这个星球上几乎每个人都经历过——最终都走了出来。

sentences.en: And if the worst case is that you are not real or the world isn't real, actually, that's not even a bad thing necessarily.
sentences.zh: 即使最坏的情况是你不是真实的，或者世界不是真实的，其实那也不一定是一件坏事。

sentences.en: You will still be okay.
sentences.zh: 你依然会没事的。

sentences.en: You can still trust yourself to get through that.
sentences.zh: 你依然可以相信自己能度过难关。

sentences.en: It's not even like that is the case.
sentences.zh: 事实甚至根本不是那样。

sentences.en: Like, when you start to really question it, like, you see how ridiculous it is.
sentences.zh: 当你开始真正质疑它时，你会发现它是多么荒谬。

sentences.en: But even the most ridiculous fears aren't really that scary if they were to actually come true.
sentences.zh: 但即使是最荒谬的恐惧，如果真的成真了，其实也没那么可怕。

sentences.en: And they weren't even.
sentences.zh: 而且它们甚至根本不会成真。

sentences.en: So, you're good on both fronts.
sentences.zh: 所以，在这两方面你都没问题。

sentences.en: I think that's all we have time for today.
sentences.zh: 我想今天的时间就到这里了。

sentences.en: I hope you enjoyed this episode.
sentences.zh: 希望你喜欢这一集。

sentences.en: I hope you learned something.
sentences.zh: 希望你学到了一些东西。

sentences.en: I hope it felt validating.
sentences.zh: 希望它让你感到被理解。

sentences.en: I hope that it's something you can come back to when you are feeling that same, like, airy, scary, panicked feeling of not being here.
sentences.zh: 希望当你再次感到那种飘忽、恐惧、恐慌的“不在这里”的感觉时，可以回想起这些内容。

sentences.en: We've all been there.
sentences.zh: 我们都经历过这些。

sentences.en: Well, at least I can say I most certainly have.
sentences.zh: 好吧，至少我可以肯定地说我经历过。

sentences.en: And I have made it through.
sentences.zh: 而且我已经走出来了。

sentences.zh: 但下次见之前，请保持安全，保持友善，善待自己。
